line.forward15-choice.speaker: General Staff
line.forward15-choice.text: The Stavka does not want to move whole armies from one end of the front to the other for the coming offensives. Your army will stay on the sector where it is committed, to the end of the war. Choose where. — Army Group North: the shortest road. Lift the siege of Leningrad and follow the Germans into Courland. — Army Group Centre: the hardest. Smolensk, Belorussia, the Vistula and finally Berlin - or something worse, if our allies in the west play us false. — Army Group South: the longest. The Kuban bridgehead first, then the Ukraine, Romania and Hungary, all the way to Prague. — Two of these roads will not end in Europe. There is still Japan to settle.
line.forward15-choice.choice.forward15-c: Smolensk, Belorussia and the Vistula. The road ends in Berlin - or in a new war against the Western Allies.
The Kuban bridgehead, the Ukraine, Romania and Hungary. The road ends in Prague, and then in Manchuria.
Lift the siege of Leningrad, then Vyborg, Riga and Courland. The road ends in Courland, and then in Manchuria.
